Your W-2 status is not the end of the planning conversation.

A familiar checklist may be a starting point, but high-income physicians often need a wider, coordinated review.

Perspective from Gary Kauffman
Founder, DWP Consulting

High-income W-2 physicians are often told that their options begin and end with workplace retirement contributions and a small set of familiar accounts. Those steps may be useful, but they do not answer every planning question created by a complex financial life.

Start with coordination, not a tactic

Tax decisions should be evaluated beside cash-flow needs, investment concentration, charitable intent, estate structure, business interests, and the timing of retirement. A tactic that appears attractive in isolation may create a different result when the wider plan is considered.

Questions to bring to the team

  • Are retirement contributions being evaluated alongside future distribution exposure?
  • Do charitable intentions and appreciated assets appear in the same planning conversation?
  • Are supplemental income, consulting work, or ownership interests changing the analysis?
  • Is investment tax management coordinated with the CPA’s year-round projections?
  • Are proposed strategies documented with assumptions, tradeoffs, costs, and responsible professionals?

Planning is not a promise

Tax rules and individual circumstances change. The goal is not to assume that every physician has access to the same strategy. It is to make sure the team has examined the relevant questions before concluding that no further coordination is available.

Source perspective

This original educational article was informed by a recent public LinkedIn newsletter discussion from Gary Kauffman about planning questions for high-income W-2 physicians.
